messages:
support-ryan: FYI — Customer (James) opened an escalation: streaming endpoints seem fine for total latency but p95/p99 TTFB spikes ~2-3x during bursts. Non-streaming endpoints don’t show the same first-byte lag. request id cid=8f7b22. Posting repro and quick logs below so we can triage.

support-ryan: Repro steps (from customer):
1) curl against /v1/stream with h2 via our proxy: `curl --http2 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d @prompt.json`
2) measure time of first chunk vs final chunk. They see first chunk at ~300-500ms p50 but p95 ~2.2s, p99 ~4.1s. Non-streaming `POST /v1/generate-sync` p95 for first byte ~220ms.

support-ryan: They ran a minimal python client too (httpx) streaming read and saw the same distribution. Paste of chunk timing excerpt from their capture (timestamps are ms offset):
```
0.0ms - connect
180.3ms - request headers sent
310.6ms - first chunk (\"data: {\"token\":\"Hello\"}\")
2300.1ms - second chunk
4100.7ms - final flush
```

alex-m: Thanks Ryan. First-pass questions: which proxy path is this hitting (edge nginx -> envoy -> runtime?), and any recent changes to http2 window/flowcontrol or our chunk coalescing heuristic? Also does the client show retransmits or rtt spikes?

support-ryan: Customer is in us-west with our standard edge stack: nginx-edge (TLS terminate) -> envoy-frontend (http/2) -> internal proxy -> runtime pool. No config changes on customer side. We rolled a small change to envoy's max-concurrent-streams and http2 connection pooling 2 days ago (eng-releases ticket ENG-1824).

lina-eng: Noted. Hypothesis: http2 PRIORITY/flow control interplay + edge TCP coalescing could delay first chunk when payload small. Also our streaming runtime default flush threshold is 4 tokens / 8ms — we backpressure to batch. Under bursty arrival, batches might get buffered longer due to downstream flow control.

sre-oncall: Can we get tcpdump from the edge and capture server push windows? Also check nginx proxy_buffering/off for the route. If nginx turns on buffer, small writes will be coalesced.

support-ryan: Customer provided nginx conf — buffer on, proxy_buffer_size 8k, proxy_buffers 4 8k. They are using SSE wrapper in browser but replicates with curl/httpx. They also captured netstat showing increased send queue at p95.

alex-m: Two lines of investigation:
- infra: look at edge config (nginx buffering, tcp_nodelay/Nagle), envoy http2 window sizes and our connection pool rollout ENG-1824.
- runtime: add temporary debug logs for chunk flush times and what triggered flush (time-based vs token-based vs forced end).

lina-eng: I'll add runtime debug flag to log \"flush_reason\" and token count per flush; can flip for a single customer pool. This will tell us if flushes are delayed waiting for batch size.

incidents-bot: runbook note created: incident/streaming-ttfb-investigation-2030001234. Assigned to lina-eng.

support-ryan: Customer willing to test quick mitigations: (A) force non-streaming route for this customer until we fix, (B) reduce nginx proxy_buffering and tcp coalescing at edge, (C) set runtime flush threshold to lower value for their pool.

lina-eng: I pushed a small change to runtime to temporarily reduce token flush threshold from 4 -> 1 for the customer's dedicated pool (will be live in 10m). Also enabled debug flush_reason logs.

alex-m: Meanwhile I'll spin up an envoy test with the prior connection-pool config and compare behavior. If ENG-1824 changed pooling, it might have increased connection reuse causing head-of-line blocking across streams under HTTP/2.

support-ryan: Customer tried option (A) — non-streaming route — and reported first-byte p95 dropped to ~240ms. So this isolates the issue to streaming path. They also tried (B) setting proxy_buffering off and saw immediate improvement (p95 ~300ms).

lina-eng: Runtime debug logs show majority of first-flushes are flagged as \"time_window_wait\" at ~150-400ms, not token_count. So flush is waiting for upstream event — likely agent-level coalescing after write syscalls. Suggests edge/proxy buffering or TCP coalescing.

sre-oncall: Ok that points to line-rate / socket buffering. Can we confirm if tcp_nodelay is set at nginx and envoy? Nagle can create these multi-hundred-ms delays for small writes.

alex-m: Checked nginx config on edge and confirm tcp_nodelay was accidentally disabled in a patch (nginx 1.21 compile flag mismatch). That explains why small chunk writes are being coalesced until buffer full or timer expiry. Patch rolled 2 days ago matches timing of regression.

support-ryan: Nice find. Customer is on a path where tcp_nodelay was relied upon. We should prepare rollback or targeted fix.

lina-eng: Immediate mitigations:
- Turn tcp_nodelay back on at nginx (hot reload) for streaming routes (low risk).
- Add an interim runtime config override to force flush on first token (we already set to 1 for testing).
- Document recommended proxy settings for SSE/h2 streaming clients.

sre-oncall: I'll coordinate the nginx reload in us-west edge and monitor p95. Will also check if other regions got same nginx build.

support-ryan: Customer confirmed after nginx tcp_nodelay fix p95 TTFB went to ~260ms and p99 reduced from 4.1s -> 1.1s. They are happy with temporary fix.

lina-eng: Follow-ups:
- ENG-1824 revert? we still need that pooling change, but we should make sure tcp_nodelay+envoy settings are compatible.
- Add runtime telemetry for flush_reason aggregated per customer to detect regressions early.
- Update docs: proxy_buffering off, tcp_nodelay on, recommended keepalive and window sizes for streaming.

alex-m: Also run a controlled canary: enable new nginx build globally only after tcp_nodelay is on and we have flush telemetry.

support-ryan: Closing notes for on-call: customer left positive feedback. I'm leaving the ticket open until ENG-1824 compatibility pass and docs PR. Action items assigned: lina-eng (telemetry + docs), alex-m (envoy test + canary plan), sre-oncall (edge nginx rollout and audit).

support-ryan: cc @customer-james thanks for quick tests and providing tcpdumps — saved a lot of time. :thumbsup:

customer-james: Thanks team — much better now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

sre-oncall: Marking incident resolved after 4h monitoring with stable p99. Will post postmortem summary tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

lina-eng: PMing a short postmortem draft in #postmortems today with links to configs, logs, and the telemetry query used.
